delegations.brief:
[MonoCode brief from Tally lead]

Ash asked for a change to MonoCode Hub itself: "Ash's words, verbatim: "inbox rows r still too tall on the laptop. the settings page scrolls weird. want a shortcut for a new chat. terminal font is tiny. notes shud sync between windows. let me pin a chat to the top. the rail badge doesnt clear after i answer something. today shud show what finished overnight at the top. make the send button not jump when the text wraps. teh model picker forgets my pick after restart. add a little undo after archive. dark mode the code blocks r unreadable. search in a chat would be nice. being built list shud group by project not by time. the archive button sits too close to delete. and the dock icon badge is wrong half the time." New-chat shortcut: he did not name the keys; use ⌘N. One part per ask. Do not post anything."
Make it in /private/var/folders/b4/8qh0t36j0_g9srqzx1g5t3z40000gn/T/monocode-realtest-eWN39Z/home/Library/Application Support/com.ash.monocode-hub.dev.cos-r62-realtest/hub-changes/hc-mvvxt01p3445, a preview copy of the hub's own code. The running hub doesn't change until Ash clicks Apply.
One git commit per separate part of the ask, each subject a few plain words Ash can read ("New chat button is at the top").
Only how the app looks and works on a screen can change here: src/ and public/, but not the engine (src/integrations, src/platform, src/features/sessions/model, src/features/hub/model, src/features/agent-app), Settings, keys, the Monos list or src/main.tsx. Those need a real build and go to the MonoCode Hub lead; the app refuses them here, so say so plainly if the ask needs one.
Use the theme tokens for colour. Run npx tsc --noEmit and the tests of what you touched, then report each commit in one line.
